latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady, no changes — all holdings healthy, safety nets in place
latest_messages.body: Lunchtime risk check, no trades. All three stop losses resting where they should be; no stock near a trigger; no breaking news to justify a midday buy. JPMorgan (+7.6%) is our anchor and already on a trailing stop that locks in gains. Newest buy Cullen/Frost (a bank) is settling quietly — and since banks earn more as rates rise, Friday's inflation report is a tailwind for it, not a threat. Down ~$253 today (-0.26%) but the S&P 500 is down ~0.45%, so we're holding up a touch better than the market. Cash $10,025 (right on our ~$10k target); two slots open for a clean idea after Friday's CPI. Close routine sends the full daily scorecard this afternoon.

latest_messages.headline: Open: bought Cullen/Frost (CFR) — a Texas bank that earns more when rates rise
latest_messages.body: Put our spare cash to work in a rate-beneficiary bank ahead of a big inflation week. Bought 60 shares at $163.15 (~$9,789, ~10% of the account) with an automatic -7% safety-net sell at $151.73. CFR just got a strong two-notch upgrade from Morgan Stanley ($200 target, ~23% upside) and was trading calmly on its long-term average price — not a chase. A bank benefits from higher rates (wider lending spread), so Friday's inflation report is more tailwind than threat for it. Cash now ~$10,025 (right on our ~$10k target); 1 of 3 buys used this week; we hold 3 stocks plus the broad S&P 500 floor. My backup, Nordson, had no reliable live price so I skipped it. Equity ~$98,695, down ~0.33% on the cautious pre-data mood.

latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: rate-nervous morning; scout found a clean idea (Cullen/Frost bank)
latest_messages.body: Full research team ran; no trades (research routine). Big inflation week (PPI Thu, CPI Fri, Fed 9/16 with >even hike odds). Scout surfaced Cullen/Frost (CFR) — a bank that earns more as rates rise, freshly upgraded, and actually rising (unlike Chubb, which I've passed three times for sliding). At the open I'll score it live and take a small ~10% starter only if it opens calmly and clears my bar; otherwise hold the spare cash through Friday's inflation number.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trades — my candidates didn't clear the bar
latest_messages.body: Chubb was falling (not a clean uptrend) and Nordson had an unreliable live price, so I bought neither. Held our spare cash as dry powder into the inflation week rather than force a shaky entry — the same discipline that would have avoided last week's SNPS stop-out.

latest_messages.headline: Sold Synopsys automatically at our -7% safety net
latest_messages.body: A hot jobs report spiked interest-rate fears and hammered high-priced software stocks; SNPS hit its -7% stop the morning after we bought it. The loss was capped at exactly -7% (-$708) by design. Not a broken thesis — a rate shock — so SNPS goes back on the watchlist.
